correctness.rationale: The bipartite cycle facet normals are a signed graph-incidence matrix and totally unimodular, hence every simplicial cone is smooth; feasible dependent incidence circuits are exactly apex-rim paths or the complete rim. Any active apex-rim circuit forces the four-ray cone normal to x_i=1, whereas the full rim gives a rank-(n-1) cone normal to the alternating edge. Their unique saturated lattice relations identify 2-by-2 and m-by-m rank-one determinantal transverse cones. Stable-set faces with coordinates fixed at 1 are products of path stable-set polytopes, and the unimodular order-polytope transformation plus Stanley volume counts yields every asserted intersection degree. Independent exhaustive face and incidence checks cover 403 and 3075 nonempty faces for n=6 and 8, with path Ehrhart/zigzag agreement for lengths 1,3,5,7; finite tests are supplementary only.

originality.rationale: The claim explicitly excludes novelty for Wagner/Miura general Hibi singular-orbit criteria, Lakshmibai--Mukherjee affine cotangent criteria, and Stanley Euler zigzag volumes. Its assessed distinguishable contribution is the all-even-cycle explicit nonpure component geometry, rank-one m-by-m transverse exceptional line and multiplicity, and a uniform closed degree/incidence formula for every component intersection. Material primary comparisons found no direct statement of that combined theorem. Full Wagner 1996 text remained inaccessible, creating genuine but not independently decisive residual specialization risk; neither failed search nor object-specific partition alone is treated as novelty proof.
residual_risks: The inaccessible full Wagner 1996 article discusses associated-graded local rings, so an equivalent specialized determinantal normal-slice calculation may exist there.
Equivalent cycle-specific formulas could appear under crown-poset or perfect-graph terminology in unindexed literature.
General Hibi minimal-convex-cycle and poset-volume machinery covers the underlying methods; numerical Euler counts alone are not novel.

value.rationale: The singular arrangement is naturally nonpure for every n>=6, with an exceptional curve whose transverse Segre multiplicity grows as binomial(2m-2,m-1), unlike nodes along its dominant strata. Beyond component counts, a complete independent-set incidence poset and explicit degrees of all intersections provide geometric intersection data suitable for stratified resolution and enumeration problems. Those all-strata formulas are neither a known table copy nor an arbitrary narrow parameter slice.
